question: Should the iOS Share Extension block the entire share whenever selected attachments cannot all be delivered, rather than preserving partial delivery with supported attachments?
rationale: The implementation is correct and well proven, but it deliberately changes an existing user workflow from partial delivery to requiring the user to remove unsupported or over-limit items.

options.title: Block omitted content
options.body: Accept the PR’s fail-closed behavior so a share cannot silently deliver only a subset of the selected attachments.

options.title: Confirm partial delivery
options.body: Preserve the ability to send supported attachments only after showing the omission summary and receiving explicit user confirmation.

options.title: Wait for transport expansion
options.body: Pause the change until the share and gateway paths support additional attachment types or a higher image limit.

recommendation.title: Block omitted content
recommendation.body: Accept the PR’s fail-closed behavior so a share cannot silently deliver only a subset of the selected attachments.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available iOS-area history signal and provided the native proof needed to evaluate this behavior choice.
